overall: Board violated the OML by creating insufficient minutes for Oct 11, Dec 11, and Dec 18, 2023 meetings; no violation for June 21 and Nov 13 minutes or document lists; intentional violation declined. Board ordered to revise minutes and certify within 60 days.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the June 21, 2023 minutes lacked sufficient detail of discussions and actions taken during the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Since this meeting was brief and the minutes capture the substance of the discussion and actions of the Board, we find that the minutes of this meeting are sufficient and that a member of the public could read the minutes and have an understanding of what occurred during the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the October 11, December 11, and December 18, 2023 minutes lacked summaries of discussions, listing only topic phrases.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law where the minutes of the meetings held on October 11, 2023, December 11, 2023, and December 18, 2023, do not adequately capture the substance of the discussions that occurred so that a member of the public who did not attend the meeting could read the minutes and have an understanding of what occurred.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the November 13, 2023 minutes were insufficient, including the executive session convening record.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the minutes contain sufficient information where they record the procedural requirements for entering executive session and thus provide a member of the public with a clear understanding of what occurred during the meeting.

allegations.summary: The November 13, 2023 minutes recorded the executive session vote as unanimous rather than by roll call, which the AG reminded the Board to record properly.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law expressly requires not only that a roll call vote be conducted before entering executive session, but also that the roll call vote be "entered into the minutes."

allegations.summary: Complainant urged a finding that the Board's minutes violation was intentional.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to find an intentional violation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that the five sets of minutes failed to include a list of documents and exhibits used at each meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we are constrained to find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law with respect to this allegation.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: the AG reminded the Board to review and approve open session minutes in a timely manner.

remedy: Revise, to the best of its abilities, the minutes of the October 11, 2023, December 11, 2023, and December 18, 2023 meetings and certify to the AG within 60 days that it has done so.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
remedy_passage: We order the Board to revise, to the best of its abilities, these three sets of minutes and to certify to this office within sixty (60) days of the date of this letter that it has done so.
